rationale: Split into three children. The supplied proof has three independent mathematical ingredients followed by measure-theoretic bookkeeping: (i) steps 1–2, the derivative of g(y) = γ(|y−ξ|)(y−ξ), including the non-smooth centre y = ξ, where Dg(ξ) = γ(0)I. This is child radial_derivative and is genuinely new relative to SimonGMT, which uses a squared-radius field. (ii) step 3, the trace identity trace((cI + F⊗v)∘p_P) = c·dim P + F(p_P v), child projection_trace, the linear algebra behind Simon's Σe^{jj} = n and Σe^{jk}(x^j−ξ^j)(x^k−ξ^k)/r² = |p_T(x−ξ)|²/r². (iii) step 4, the pointwise formula div_M X(x) = h(nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ)) + γ(r)⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h⟩ wherever dim T_xV = n and h is differentiable at x, child pointwise_divergence, which combines (i), (ii), the product rule and the Pythagoras/self-adjointness facts (Simon 3.2, 5.1). Each is a self-contained, reusable statement: a calculus lemma, a linear-algebra lemma, and Simon's div_M formula for weighted radial fields, which other first-variation computations of radial test fields can reuse. The parent keeps only steps 5–7. Let X = h·γ(|x−ξ|)(x−ξ), a test field in U. (a) Off U, x ∉ tsupport X, so fderiv X x = 0, div_M X(x) = 0 and X(x) = 0. Hence ∫div_M X dμ = ∫_U div_M X dμ and ∫⟨X,H⟩dμ = ∫_U⟨X,H⟩dμ, using only setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, with no integrability needed. (b) For x ∈ U, h is differentiable at x (U open, h ∈ C¹(U)), and dim T_xV = n μ-a.e. So by pointwise_divergence, div_M X = Φ μ-a.e. on U, and ∫_U div_M X = ∫_U Φ by setIntegral_congr_ae; U is open, hence measurable, and no integrability is needed. (c) ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = h(x)γ(|x−ξ|)⟨x−ξ, H(x)⟩ by real_inner_smul_left. (d) HasMeanCurvatureIn applied to X gives ∫div_M X = −∫⟨X,H⟩. Combining (a)–(d) gives the exact frozen conclusion. This was verified in Lean, not just on paper: all three children and the parent were proved in a scratch file in the comparator's replayed contract scope, with the exact frozen types. The parent uses only child 3, and child 3 uses children 1 and 2. The file has no errors and its axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proof sizes are about 39, 9, 34 and 26 lines, so each child is a small, safe unit. An independent reviewer accepted the split with edits. Each child's proof now carries its own conventions paragraph. Child 3 states that fderiv ℝ X x = DX(x) by uniqueness. Child 2 records the basis-free Mathlib route. The dependencies are acyclic, and no child restates the parent or solves another DAG node.

subproblems.title: Derivative of the radial field γ(|y−ξ|)(y−ξ), including the centre (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ, Euclidean inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|), γ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, and ξ, x ∈ E; put r = |x − ξ|. Then the vector field g(y) = γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ) is Fréchet differentiable at x with derivative Dg(x)v = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ) for v ∈ E, where γ'(r)/r is read as 0 when r = 0 (Lean's a/0 = 0); in particular Dg(ξ) = γ(0)·I.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ x : Ambient n ℓ), ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → HasFDerivAt (fun y : Ambient n ℓ ↦ γ ‖y - ξ‖ • (y - ξ)) (γ ‖x - ξ‖ • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) + (deriv γ ‖x - ξ‖ / ‖x - ξ‖) • (innerSL ℝ (x - ξ)).smulRight (x - ξ)) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). γ'(t) denotes deriv γ t. innerSL ℝ w is the linear functional u ↦ ⟨w, u⟩; for a functional L and a vector w, L.smulRight w is the map u ↦ L(u)w; ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E is the identity I. HasFDerivAt g L x means g(x + v) = g(x) + L v + o(|v|) as v → 0 (Fréchet differentiability of g at x with derivative L). Notation: r = |x − ξ|, g(y) = γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ), and the claimed derivative is L_x(v) = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ).

1. Case x = ξ. Then r = 0 and x − ξ = 0. The coefficient γ'(0)/0 equals 0 and the vector x − ξ is 0, so the claimed derivative is L_ξ(v) = γ(0)v, i.e. L_ξ = γ(0)I. For v ∈ E we have g(ξ) = γ(0)·0 = 0 and g(ξ + v) = γ(|v|)v, hence g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v = (γ(|v|) − γ(0))v.
2. γ is C¹, hence continuous, and |v| → 0 as v → 0; therefore ε(v) := γ(|v|) − γ(0) → 0 as v → 0. Consequently |g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v| = |ε(v)|·|v| = o(|v|) as v → 0, which says exactly that g is Fréchet differentiable at ξ with derivative γ(0)I = L_ξ. This proves the claim when x = ξ.
3. Case x ≠ ξ, so r > 0. The map y ↦ y − ξ is differentiable at x with derivative I. The map y ↦ |y − ξ|² = ⟨y − ξ, y − ξ⟩ is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ 2⟨x − ξ, v⟩ (product rule for the inner product). Since |x − ξ|² = r² > 0 and t ↦ √t is differentiable at every t > 0 with derivative 1/(2√t), the chain rule shows that y ↦ |y − ξ| = √(|y − ξ|²) is differentiable at x with derivative v ↦ (1/(2r))·2⟨x − ξ, v⟩ = r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, v⟩.
4. γ is C¹, so it is differentiable at r with derivative γ'(r) = deriv γ r. By the chain rule, φ(y) := γ(|y − ξ|) is differentiable at x with Dφ(x)v = γ'(r)·r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, v⟩.
5. By the product rule for a real-valued function times a vector-valued function, g(y) = φ(y)·(y − ξ) is differentiable at x with Dg(x)v = φ(x)·v + (Dφ(x)v)·(x − ξ) = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ) = L_x(v), using φ(x) = γ(r) and γ'(r)·r⁻¹ = γ'(r)/r. This proves the claim when x ≠ ξ, and with step 2 the lemma is proved.
proof_key_steps: At x = ξ the claimed derivative is γ(0)I because γ'(0)/0 = 0 and x − ξ = 0
g(ξ + v) − g(ξ) − γ(0)v = (γ(|v|) − γ(0))v = o(|v|) by continuity of γ at 0
For x ≠ ξ: y ↦ |y − ξ| = √(|y − ξ|²) has derivative r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, ·⟩ (chain rule with √ at r² > 0)
Chain rule: D[γ(|y − ξ|)](x) = γ'(r) r⁻¹⟨x − ξ, ·⟩
Product rule with y ↦ y − ξ (derivative I) gives Dg(x)v = γ(r)v + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, v⟩(x − ξ)

subproblems.title: Trace of (cI + F(·)v) ∘ p_P equals c·dim P + F(p_P v)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), P ⊆ E any linear subspace with orthogonal projection p = p_P (P.starProjection), c ∈ ℝ, F : E → ℝ a continuous linear functional and v ∈ E. Then the endomorphism A = c·I + F(·)v, A(u) = c·u + F(u)·v, satisfies trace(A ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (c : ℝ) (F : Ambient n ℓ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (v : Ambient n ℓ), LinearMap.trace ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) ((c • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Ambient n ℓ) + F.smulRight v).toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = c * (Module.finrank ℝ P : ℝ) + F (P.starProjection v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). N = n + ℓ = dim E. P is an arbitrary linear subspace of E, k = dim P = Module.finrank ℝ P, and p = P.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of E onto P (p u ∈ P and u − p u ⊥ P for all u; hence p u = u for u ∈ P and p u = 0 for u ∈ P^⊥). F : E → ℝ is a continuous linear functional, c ∈ ℝ, v ∈ E, and A = c • ContinuousLinearMap.id + F.smulRight v, i.e. A(u) = c·u + F(u)·v. trace = LinearMap.trace ℝ E, and A ∘ p is the composite u ↦ A(p u) (as a linear map).

1. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_k of P and an orthonormal basis τ_{k+1}, …, τ_N of P^⊥. Since E is finite-dimensional, E = P ⊕ P^⊥ is an orthogonal direct sum, so τ_1, …, τ_N is an orthonormal basis of E.
2. For every linear map B : E → E, trace B = Σ_{j=1}^{N} ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩, because ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩ is the j-th diagonal entry of the matrix of B in the orthonormal basis (τ_j).
3. pτ_j = τ_j for j ≤ k (as τ_j ∈ P) and pτ_j = 0 for j > k (as τ_j ∈ P^⊥). Applying step 2 to B = A ∘ p gives trace(A ∘ p) = Σ_{j=1}^{k} ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩.
4. For each j ≤ k, ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩ = c⟨τ_j, τ_j⟩ + F(τ_j)⟨v, τ_j⟩ = c + F(τ_j)⟨v, τ_j⟩, since |τ_j| = 1.
5. Summing over j ≤ k and using linearity of F: trace(A ∘ p) = ck + Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩F(τ_j) = ck + F(Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j) = ck + F(p v), because the orthogonal projection onto P has the expansion p v = Σ_{j≤k} ⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j in the orthonormal basis τ_1, …, τ_k of P. Since k = dim P, this is the claim trace(A ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v).
Remark (the same computation without bases, matching Mathlib): A ∘ p = c·p + G(·)v with G = F ∘ p linear; by linearity of the trace, trace(A ∘ p) = c·trace(p) + trace(u ↦ G(u)v); trace(p) = k because p maps E onto P and fixes P (Mathlib LinearMap.IsProj.trace), and the rank-one map u ↦ G(u)v has trace G(v) = F(p v) (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_smulRight). The pinned SimonGMT library contains this identity with an extra scalar b (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold.trace_radialEndomorphism, take b = 1).
proof_key_steps: Orthonormal basis τ_1..τ_N of E with τ_1..τ_k a basis of P and τ_{k+1}..τ_N a basis of P^⊥
trace B = Σ_j ⟨Bτ_j, τ_j⟩; since pτ_j = τ_j (j ≤ k) and pτ_j = 0 (j > k), trace(A∘p) = Σ_{j≤k} ⟨Aτ_j, τ_j⟩
Sum: ck + F(Σ_{j≤k}⟨v, τ_j⟩τ_j) = c·dim P + F(p v)

subproblems.title: Pointwise tangential divergence of h·γ(|x−ξ|)(x−ξ) (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2 and 5.1)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Ambient n ℓ), V any rectifiable n-varifold in E (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ), h : E → ℝ, γ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, and ξ, x ∈ E, and suppose dim T_xV = n and h is differentiable at x. Let X(y) = (h(y)γ(|y − ξ|))(y − ξ) and r = |x − ξ|. Then div_M X(x) = h(x)(nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x))) + γ(r)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩, where div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) ∘ p_{T_xV}) (V.tangentialDiv X x), ∇^M h(x) = p_{T_xV}(∇h(x)) (V.tangentialGradient h x) and q_ξ(x) = |p_{T_xV}^⊥(x − ξ)|²/r² (V.normalRadialSq ξ x, equal to 0 when r = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ x : Ambient n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ (V.tangentSpace x) = n → DifferentiableAt ℝ h x → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → V.tangentialDiv (fun y ↦ (h y * γ ‖y - ξ‖) • (y - ξ)) x = h x * ((n : ℝ) * γ ‖x - ξ‖ + ‖x - ξ‖ * deriv γ ‖x - ξ‖ * (1 - V.normalRadialSq ξ x)) + γ ‖x - ξ‖ * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (V.tangentialGradient h x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. n, ℓ ∈ ℕ; E = Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, a finite-dimensional real inner product space with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ = inner ℝ and norm |·| = ‖·‖. Real division by 0 is 0 (Lean convention: a/0 = 0 for every a ∈ ℝ). For V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ and x ∈ E: T_xV = V.tangentSpace x is a linear subspace of E; p_x = (T_xV).starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T_xV and p_x^⊥ = (T_xV)ᗮ.starProjection the orthogonal projection onto its orthogonal complement (p_x^⊥ = I − p_x); both are self-adjoint and idempotent. For X : E → E, div_M X(x) = V.tangentialDiv X x := trace(fderiv ℝ X x ∘ p_x), where fderiv ℝ X x is the Fréchet derivative DX(x) whenever X is differentiable at x. For h : E → ℝ, ∇h(x) = gradient h x is the Riesz representative of Dh(x) = fderiv ℝ h x, i.e. ⟨∇h(x), u⟩ = Dh(x)u for all u, and ∇^M h(x) = V.tangentialGradient h x := p_x(∇h(x)). q_ξ(x) = V.normalRadialSq ξ x := |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² (= 0 when x = ξ). γ'(t) = deriv γ t. This proof uses the sibling lemmas radial_vector_field_hasFDerivAt (for γ ∈ C¹ and all ξ, x: y ↦ γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ) is differentiable at x with derivative u ↦ γ(r)u + (γ'(r)/r)⟨x − ξ, u⟩(x − ξ), r = |x − ξ|, γ'(r)/r = 0 when r = 0) and trace_scalar_add_rankOne_comp_starProjection (for every subspace P with projection p, c ∈ ℝ, linear F : E → ℝ and v ∈ E: trace((cI + F(·)v) ∘ p) = c·dim P + F(p v)).

1. Write P = T_xV, p = p_x, p^⊥ = p_x^⊥, w = x − ξ (so r = |w|), and g(y) = γ(|y − ξ|)(y − ξ). Then X(y) = (h(y)γ(|y − ξ|))(y − ξ) = h(y)·g(y) for every y, since (ab)u = a(bu).
2. By radial_vector_field_hasFDerivAt, g is differentiable at x with Dg(x)u = γ(r)u + (γ'(r)/r)⟨w, u⟩w, where γ'(r)/r = 0 if r = 0.
3. By hypothesis h is differentiable at x, with derivative Dh(x) satisfying Dh(x)u = ⟨∇h(x), u⟩. By the product rule, X = h·g is differentiable at x with DX(x)u = h(x)·Dg(x)u + (Dh(x)u)·g(x).
4. Since g(x) = γ(r)w, step 2 gives DX(x)u = (h(x)γ(r))u + F(u)w for all u, where F(u) := h(x)(γ'(r)/r)⟨w, u⟩ + γ(r)Dh(x)u is a continuous linear functional. Thus DX(x) = cI + F(·)w with c = h(x)γ(r).
5. As X is differentiable at x, fderiv ℝ X x = DX(x) (uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative), so div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) ∘ p) by definition. By trace_scalar_add_rankOne_comp_starProjection (with this P, c, F and v = w) and the hypothesis dim P = n: div_M X(x) = c·n + F(p w) = n·h(x)γ(r) + h(x)(γ'(r)/r)⟨w, p w⟩ + γ(r)Dh(x)(p w).
6. Gradient term: Dh(x)(p w) = ⟨∇h(x), p w⟩ = ⟨p∇h(x), w⟩ (p is self-adjoint) = ⟨w, ∇^M h(x)⟩.
7. Projection term: p w ∈ P, so p(p w) = p w; with self-adjointness, ⟨w, p w⟩ = ⟨w, p(p w)⟩ = ⟨p w, p w⟩ = |p w|². By Pythagoras (w = p w + p^⊥w with p w ⊥ p^⊥w), r² = |p w|² + |p^⊥w|², hence ⟨w, p w⟩ = r² − |p^⊥w|².
8. If r ≠ 0: (γ'(r)/r)(r² − |p^⊥w|²) = rγ'(r)(1 − |p^⊥w|²/r²) = rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x)). If r = 0: then w = 0, so (γ'(r)/r)⟨w, p w⟩ = 0 and rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x)) = 0. Hence in both cases h(x)(γ'(r)/r)⟨w, p w⟩ = h(x)·rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x)).
9. Substituting steps 6–8 into step 5: div_M X(x) = h(x)nγ(r) + h(x)rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x)) + γ(r)⟨w, ∇^M h(x)⟩ = h(x)(nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x))) + γ(r)⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: X = h·g with g(y) = γ(|y−ξ|)(y−ξ); Dg(x) from radial_vector_field_hasFDerivAt
Product rule: DX(x) = h(x)γ(r)I + F(·)(x−ξ) with F = h(x)(γ'(r)/r)⟨x−ξ,·⟩ + γ(r)Dh(x)
fderiv ℝ X x = DX(x); trace_scalar_add_rankOne_comp_starProjection with dim T_xV = n gives n h(x)γ(r) + F(p_x(x−ξ))
Dh(x)(p_x(x−ξ)) = ⟨x−ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩ by self-adjointness of p_x
Case r ≠ 0: (γ'(r)/r)(r² − |p^⊥(x−ξ)|²) = rγ'(r)(1 − q_ξ(x)); case r = 0: both terms vanish; combine
